note: Adapted from Sjöstedt's German description of 1904 (the alate also has a Latin diagnosis). Sjöstedt himself notes that the species belongs to the Palaearctic Region and gives only a brief account here, referring to the monograph of Grassi & Sandias for the detailed study; the distribution is given as the Mediterranean coast, Algiers in North Africa and Egypt. The original gives wing length and wing width side by side with resp. (respectively), and they are listed here item by item. The OCR text of the archive.org scan was used, in which two figures were misread (wing expanse 18, body length including the wings 10) and have been restored from the context.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Black or dark chestnut brown throughout; antennae, mouthparts, legs and pronotum yellow, the pronotum sometimes darker behind. Head nearly rounded-square; compound eyes small and circular, not much projecting; ocelli very small, situated very close to the compound eyes. Pronotum large, transversely rectangular, the sides strongly bent down, their corners rounded, the middle of the posterior margin slightly concave. Wings transparent, slightly tinged with dark smoky, with a purple-red and green iridescence. Measurements: wing expanse 18—21 mm, body length including the wings 10—12 mm, wing length 8—9.5 mm, width 2 mm, body length (with the head) 6—7 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: In the dry specimen the head is yellowish brown, slightly darker in front, long and cylindrical, dropping steeply just before the mandibles; the front of the head has an impression that continues towards the mouth as a flattened and widened groove. Clypeus small, transversely rectangular, twice as wide as long; the right mandible has a tooth right at the base, the left mandible 3 broad teeth without a clear boundary. Antennae 16—18-segmented, segment 1 slightly constricted, segment 2 short, segment 3 as long as segment 1 and inverted-conical; a small compound eye just behind the antenna, evident only under fairly strong magnification; the underside of the head with a broad median area. Pronotum as wide as the head, transversely quadrangular, the sides bent down, the anterior margin concave; mesonotum of the same shape but only half as long; metanotum shorter still and of the same shape. Body length 7—9 mm, head with the mandibles 4 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Yellow, the head as in the alate; antennae 14—16-segmented; compound eyes rather large, with facets, concolorous with the surroundings and therefore not easily noticed. Pronotum slightly wider than the head, transversely quadrangular, the sides strongly bent down, the corners nearly right-angled and slightly rounded; mesonotum and metanotum of the same shape as the pronotum but shorter; the whole body widening gradually from the pronotum backwards; wing pads small and triangular, pressed down against the thorax and not visible from above. Body length 4—6 mm.
